archer push up.name: Archer Push Up
archer push up.rawDescription:
Learn how to do an Archer Push-Up. This is an excellent chest stabilization exercise or dynamic warm-up movement.

Assume a push up position with the body in a straight line from head to heel and feet hip to shoulder width. Position one hand at an approximate 1.5-2x shoulder width position with the other hand extended out to the side with a slight bend in the elbow and hand atop a medicine ball with fingers pointing to the side. Brace the core and tighten the glutes. 

Press away from the floor to prevent the shoulder blades from winging. Lower the chest toward the floor gliding the body toward bent arm through a maximum range of motion until the chest is approximately a few inches off the floor or shoulders have reached elbow depth. Reverse the pattern and return to starting position. 

Repeat. Maintain posture throughout. Keep the shoulders from elevating or rounding. Do not let the back round or arch or the hips sag or pike. Avoid letting the head jut forward.

box jump up with stabilization.rawDescription:
The Box Jump-Up with Stabilization is a plyometric stabilization exercise. Watch this video to learn how to correctly perform this exercise.

Stand in front of a box or platform with feet shoulders-width apart and toes and knees pointed straight ahead. Squat slightly as if sitting in a chair. Using arms, jump up and land on top of box, keeping toes pointed straight ahead and knees directly over the toes. Hold for 3 to 5 seconds. Land softly with the ankles, knees, and hips flexed. Note: hips and knees will be flexed to a deeper level than the prior exercise. Do not let the client “stick” the landing with the legs straight. Step off box and repeat as instructed. 

As a progression, perform this drill by jumping laterally in the frontal plane to the top of the box. As a progression from the frontal plane box jump-up, perform in the transverse plane, rotating 90 degrees in the air before landing. You can find both of these progressions, as well as hundreds of other exercises, in the video library on NASM EDGE. Download the app at: https://nasm-edge.app.link/6Hangr8SuR.

kettlebell jerk.rawDescription:
In this video, learn how to properly do a Kettlebell Jerk. Kettlebell training has many great benefits for  individuals who wish to increase all aspects of health and fitness.

Start in a squat position with both arms extended onto each kettlebell. Quickly pull the kettlebells in between your legs and then quickly swing forward to a rack position by extending your hips and knees and bringing the kettlebells by your chest, shoulders, and biceps. Bend your knees and lift your feet off of the ground, using your body to drive the weight above your head so your arms are extended and locked. Bring your arms back down while simultaneously bending your hips and knees. Then, straighten your legs. Repeat the entire sequence again for the desired number of repetitions.

kettlebell crush curl with squat.name: Kettlebell Crush Curl With Squat
kettlebell crush curl with squat.rawDescription:
Squat into a deep squat position with feet wider than shoulder width and toes rotated slightly out. Lock shoulder blades back and down and brace core. Grip the kettlebell bottoms up (upside down) with handle positioned between forearms and hands wrapped around the bell. 

Slowly lower the kettlebell performing a bicep curl. Once elbows have reached full extension, reverse the pattern and curl the weight up to the chest through a full range. Repeat. 

Maintain posture throughout. Minimize shoulder forward roll or elbow swing behind or in front of body. Do not bottom out on the squat or let the hamstrings rest on the calves.

- Keep your elbows close to your body. 
- Start squatting by pushing your heels into the ground while sitting your hips back into a 90 degree bend at the hips and knees. 
- Keep the kettlebell at chest height and your chest up. 
- Return to the starting position. 
- Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand on a box or platform with feet shoulders-width apart and pointed straight ahead. tuck jump with stabilization.name: Tuck Jump With Stabilization
tuck jump with stabilization.rawDescription:
Do you want to learn how to do a Tuck Jump with Stabilization? Here's how to correctly perform this exercise.

Stand with your feet hip-to-shoulder width apart and pointed straight ahead. Squat slightly as if sitting in a chair. Jump up, bringing both knees toward the chest. Try to have your thighs parallel with the ground. Land softly with the whole foot and keep weight evenly distributed from heel to toe, keeping the feet, knees, and hips pointing straight ahead. Avoid landing only on balls of the feet. Hold landing for 2 seconds to stabilize. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
